insight.title: The Instant Cringe Effect
insight.subtitle: The rapid shift from novel to exhausted defines how we consume and discard digital culture.

sections.text: Viral trends have a hyper-accelerated lifecycle. A new sound or meme explodes into ubiquity, then swiftly collapses into exhaustion, often within days.
This isn't just natural evolution; it's the internet's insatiable appetite. Platforms reward constant novelty, churning content until every drop of freshness is squeezed out and discarded.
The result is a culture of instant digital archaeology. What was fresh last Tuesday now feels tragically passé. We're all chasing the next wave before the current one even fully breaks.

news.title: Cuba suffers second nationwide blackout in five days

alternates.title: EU orders Meta to fix addictive Facebook and Instagram design or face fines
